key_insight: The paper introduces a framework that uses topological conjugacy to transform free‑boundary (moving-domain) PDEs into fixed‑domain problems that neural operators can learn reliably, then maps predictions back to the original domain.
problem_solved: Neural operators have difficulty learning mappings for problems whose spatial domain or topology evolves (free/moving boundaries). This work enables operator learning for such problems (e.g., glacier melt) by removing the moving‑domain obstacle.
method: Construct a topological conjugacy (a bijective mapping) between the free‑boundary problem and an equivalent fixed‑domain formulation.
Train a neural operator on the transformed fixed‑domain PDE where standard operator learning is effective.
Use the inverse conjugacy to map learned solutions back to the original moving domain for physical interpretation and prediction.
impact: By enabling neural operators to handle evolving domains, the approach broadens the applicability of operator learning to real‑world physical systems (glaciology, fluid interfaces, phase change) and can improve efficiency and accuracy of surrogate models used in simulation and forecasting.
